methodological_rigor.justification: Solid case-control design with unmatched cohort (potential selection bias), multivariate GLM with AIC model selection, appropriate statistical methods. Methods section comprehensive. Minor limitation: unmatched case-control introduces potential confounding; acknowledged by authors.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Individual case-control study examining PCa risk factors in Tanzanian population. Directly informs prevention strategies for LMIC settings. Novel AIC ranking approach in African context strengthens clinical relevance but findings confirmatory of known dietary/lifestyle associations.

reporting_quality.justification: Comprehensive Methods and Results sections following STROBE guidelines. Clear table presentations of results with multiple statistical models. Minor gap: data/code availability statement absent. No mention of repository or sharing mechanism.

novelty_literature.justification: Novel application of AIC-based ranking to identify most important PCa risk factor classes in African population. Confirms known dietary protective factors (coffee, tomato, soya) and risk factors (red meat, alcohol) from literature. Provides region-specific evidence for LMIC context.

writing_presentation.justification: Well-organized manuscript with clear progression through demographic, lifestyle, dietary, and disease exposure factors. Figures and tables effectively communicate findings. Discussion contextualizes results within literature. Minor: some sections could be more concise.

key_strengths: Novel AIC-based ranking approach quantifying relative importance of PCa risk factor groups
Comprehensive multivariate analysis addressing dietary, lifestyle, sociodemographic, disease exposure, and family history domains
Appropriate for LMIC setting with directly actionable prevention strategies
Adequate sample size (170) with detailed statistical modeling including pseudo-R² and AUC metrics
key_concerns: Unmatched case-control design introduces selection bias; no PSM or stratification reported
Recall bias from questionnaire-based data collection inherent to case-control method
Single-center study from Dar es Salaam limits generalizability to rural or other urban African settings
Data availability not discussed; reproducibility compromised
chief_reviewer.rationale: Solid epidemiological work providing region-specific evidence on PCa risk factors through novel analytical approach. Methodological rigor appropriate for case-control design despite selection bias. Clinical relevance high for LMIC prevention strategies but not practice-changing. Tier 3 appropriate.
